To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: recruiting-ops@searchbridge.co
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Headcount scenario heatmap & req queue for QBR

Team —

Attached is the heatmap I pulled together for the QBR prep (sheet V3). It consolidates the three scenarios we discussed last week: baseline (no new hires), constrained (freeze non-critical reqs), and growth (accelerate top-priority ICs). I also attached a snapshot of the current req queue.

High-level asks: 
- Vanessa: please confirm the two backfill reqs we flagged as "time-sensitive" (REQ-4210, REQ-4321) and whether we have any sponsor/exec blockers.
- Markus: finance needs an estimate of the incremental monthly run-rate for each scenario (salary + benefits + infra delta). Can you provide a delta table by EOW?
- Laura & Connor: hiring pipeline — are there candidates we can convert quickly for the backfills? If so, note time-to-offer estimate.

I put a proposed freeze list (low-impact roles) on the last tab; the intention is to limit new requisitions to mission-critical and customer-facing infra for this quarter. We can surface exceptions in the QBR but want a conservative baseline.

Attachments: headcount_heatmap_v3.xlsx, req_queue_qbr_snapshot.pdf

Thanks — I want to lock the slides by Wednesday so the exec deck has consistent assumptions.

— Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for pulling this together. Quick read-through and a couple of notes: 

- Backfills: REQ-4210 (Senior Infra Engineer) is green — we have two strong on-site candidates, target OOO offer by 1/7 if approvals clear. REQ-4321 (CS Manager) has a stalled sign-off from Aurelia Health (stakeholder needs a 30-min sync). I've copied Kate Ellis from Aurelia to coordinate.
- Freeze list: recruiting_ops agrees with the proposed freeze except for REQ-4399 (security infra), which we recommend keep-open due to upcoming compliance deadlines.
- Pipeline: attached candidate_pipeline_summary.csv with stage breakdown; I highlighted ~6 candidates who could be converted within 2–3 weeks for internal backfills.

Notes / next steps:
1) If execs approve the constrained scenario, we can hold new req postings immediately and run a 2-week accelerated convert path for the 6 highlighted candidates.
2) For exceptions (security infra), we request a one-time headcount carve-out approval.

Vanessa

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: finance-ops@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Headcount scenario heatmap & req queue for QBR

Folks — I've run preliminary numbers. See below (summary), full delta table attached to my workbook; I'll drop the final CFO-ready slide by EOD Tuesday.

Summary (monthly incremental run-rate):
- Baseline (no hires): $0
- Constrained (approve time-sensitive backfills only): +$48k/mo (two hires)
- Growth (accelerate top-priority 6 hires): +$160k/mo

Key assumptions: median comp by band, 25% benefits load, immediate infra consumption ramp over 2 months for high-CPU workloads. If we keep security infra req (REQ-4399) open, add ~+$18k/mo.

I recommend we present two alternatives to execs: (A) constrained with single carve-out for security (lower near-term burn, preserves compliance), (B) growth with accelerated conversion (higher near-term burn, faster product velocity). Decision point will be whether compliance risk warrants the carve-out.

-Markus
Head of Finance Planning
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: finance_delta_table_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
